storylines.title: US-Ukraine rift over Starlink and strikes
storylines.summary: Trump defended waiving Russia sanctions, saying it keeps Moscow at the table, and said Zelenskyy does not want peace. Critics in both parties object; Zelenskyy spoke with US envoys. Starlink limits spur calls for investigation. Ukraine struck St Petersburg with over 1,000 drones.

events.text: Rep. Mike Turner calls for an investigation into Ukraine's temporary loss of military Starlink access.
Trump defends waiving Russia sanctions as keeping Moscow at the table and says Zelenskyy 'doesn't want to end this war.'
Zelenskyy says Ukraine trusts the US and hopes Trump changes his decisions; Bessent calls his Starlink claims reckless.
Wright calls the diesel deal a peace incentive while Rubio says Russia would sell the fuel anyway.
FT reports St Petersburg endured its biggest Ukrainian drone attack, hitting tech infrastructure.
US ambassador Puzder warns Europe of retaliation over plans to limit spectrum access for non-EU firms such as Starlink, the FT reports.
Pence urges Trump to restore Russia sanctions; Energy Secretary Wright defends the waiver as not an economic lifeline.
Zelenskyy speaks with Witkoff and Kushner, the first senior call since tensions began.
Ukraine launches more than 1,000 drones at Russia, hitting St Petersburg oil sites and a data centre; at least one killed.
Video shows explosions in St Petersburg after a suspected Ukrainian drone swarm.
Republicans and Democrats criticize Trump's sanctions waiver; Schumer calls it a gift to Putin, while Massie praises it.
Zelenskyy says Ukraine is ready to negotiate and the American negotiating track will continue.
Zelenskyy calls the sanctions waiver a 'reward' for Putin; Sen. Tillis calls it 'beyond irresponsible.'
Zelenskyy says Starlink limits in Ukraine are a 'planned operation' that hamper drone interception.
Russian strikes kill at least eight and injure nearly 60 across Ukraine.
Trump signs an order waiving Russia sanctions and tariffs mandated by a new law, a week after a diesel deal with Putin.
Italy's defense minister tells the BBC the US is wrong to restrict Ukraine support.
Four Republican senators join Democrats pressing the Pentagon on whether it ordered Ukraine Starlink restrictions.
Trump says neither he nor Musk caused the Starlink slowdown and he doesn't know who ordered the Starshield throttle.
Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi retakes more territory in Donetsk, with Starlink playing a key role, the BBC reports.

storylines.title: AI debt worries and market selloff
storylines.summary: Big Tech, chip and bank stocks are sliding as credit markets question the AI debt buildup. Asian chip stocks fell again Monday on funding worries and a DeepSeek model, while US futures rebounded. Options traders brace for a VIX surge.

events.text: Asian chip stocks fall again as DeepSeek's latest model and AI financing worries hit demand expectations.
Bloomberg says Treasuries show tentative haven signs, threatening big short bets as the AI trade wobbles.
Option traders brace for a VIX surge as accelerating inflation and AI jitters jolt stocks.
Microsoft pulls out of Nscale's Essex AI datacentre project over power supply concerns.
FT reports America's $10 trillion AI infrastructure boom is running into the economics of the physical world.
Junk bond buyers freeze out tech startups as CoreWeave's pain raises questions over AI financing.
S&P 500 tech sector has its worst week in 18 months while the average stock gains.
Software and semiconductor stocks fall together Friday on AI and interest-rate fears.
Anthropic offers Blackstone a double-digit yield on chip financing, complicating its investment-grade goal.
Big Tech posts its biggest weekly drop since 'liberation day'; CoreWeave falls 25% for the week as investors buy Treasuries.
Chip stocks near longest losing run since 2008; big bank shares on worst weekly streak since 2008.

storylines.title: Fed under Warsh weighs further hikes
storylines.summary: After a September hike, the Fed under Chairman Kevin Warsh is expected to hold Oct. 28, though MarketWatch says it is a closer call than markets think, given inflation and communication changes.

events.text: MarketWatch says the October decision is a closer call than markets think, weighing arguments against a hike.
Warsh says the economy has performed largely as expected since the September hike; markets expect a hold.

storylines.title: 2026 midterm elections
storylines.summary: Polls show Trump approval at new lows and Democrats leading the generic ballot by 8 to 10 points, per Axios. Inflation worries Republicans, early voting is underway, and the Texas Senate race draws attention as the Chamber endorses Paxton.

events.text: US Chamber of Commerce endorses Ken Paxton over James Talarico as both hold rallies before Texas early voting begins Monday.
Axios reports Beshear faces criticism from Latino lawmakers and potential 2028 rivals over Texas funding.
Axios reports three polls show Trump approval at new lows and Democrats leading by 8 to 10 points.
Troy Jackson says he won't apologize for telling Collins to 'shut up'; Angie Nixon defends calling for Moody's jailing.
Axios reports Democrats are competitive in long-Republican territory; the FT says GOP insiders think wave predictions are overstated.
FT says voters increasingly link rising energy prices to Trump administration policies.
Vance says he will decide on a 2028 run after the midterms, at a CBS town hall in Michigan.
Susquehanna poll shows Rep. Scott Perry trailing Democrat Janelle Stelson 49 percent to 46 in Pennsylvania.
Trump rallies in Kentucky for Ed Gallrein before a seven-day, seven-stop campaign tour including Michigan on Oct. 25.
The Hill says September CPI inflation of 3.7 percent adds pressure on Republicans as early voting begins.
Graham Platner's campaign spent about $2.3 million since leaving the Maine Senate race, with none going to Troy Jackson, the Washington Examiner reports.
Rep. Hillary Scholten says she got a threatening letter claiming to be from DSA, joining other lawmakers.
NPR says Trump's midterm travel includes many red states; Politico says some GOP candidates avoid featuring him.
Trump says California election officials who count noncitizen ballots will go to jail; DOJ already sued the state.
More lawmakers report suspicious mailings after earlier letters with unknown substances reached election offices.
At a Georgia rally Trump repeats a claim Ossoff's election was illegitimate; the Guardian calls it false.
Ocasio-Cortez gives $1 million to Abdul El-Sayed's Michigan Senate bid; Trump rallies in Georgia for Mike Collins.
Cook Political Report moves 11 House races toward Democrats; Talarico's haul tops Senate GOP rivals.
Musk gave a record $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund.

storylines.title: US-Iran war and oil prices
storylines.summary: After nine months of war, Brent hit $110 before easing from a five-month high. Tankers have hit mines in Hormuz and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia intensify. Trump endorsed Netanyahu; Iran's foreign minister warns Tehran has 'unfinished jobs' too.

events.text: Iran's Araghchi warns the US against renewed attack, saying Tehran has 'unfinished jobs' too.
GCC ministers condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as Yemen fighting displaces more than 233,000 people.
Bessent says oil prices falling before year-end will depend on the Iran conflict; Wright defends gas price record.
Trump says Netanyahu needs re-election or the US will have to 'finish the job' against Iran alone, per Fox News.
Trump endorses Netanyahu for reelection, calling him a critical ally against Iran, nine days before Israel's Oct. 27 election.
Iran's IRGC says two tankers, each carrying about two million barrels, caught fire after hitting mines on an unauthorised route.
Saudi-led coalition intercepts four drones over Riyadh and other areas as Egypt weighs sending help.
Iranian state TV airs video it says shows an oil tanker exploding after hitting a naval mine in Hormuz.
US and Iran both claim control of Hormuz as two vessels are struck by naval mines this week.
Vance publicly hints at disagreement with Trump over the Iran war, per the Washington Examiner.
IRGC says an oil supertanker hit a naval mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz.
CENTCOM commander says the US naval blockade has cost Iran about $25 billion in oil revenue.
Brent crude hits $110 for the first time since May amid reports Saudi-led forces intercepted missiles aimed at energy hubs.
CENTCOM's Adm. Brad Cooper says Iran-backed militias are sending money to the IRGC after nine months of war.
